correctness.rationale: The source's explicit witness bounds were reconstructed to obtain a computable obstruction bound; finite amalgamability was shown decidable using the explicit size of free exponent-three Burnside groups; joint embedding via direct products was checked before deriving completeness; and complete computable enumerability was then used for the decision procedure.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source states model-companion existence and quantitative bounded witnesses but not decidability. Repeated searches also located Lipparini's locally finite model-companion criterion, Burris's 1984 primitive-recursive result for finitely generated universal Horn classes, and Burris's 1989 decidable-model-companion criterion. No published source was found stating the exponent-three application; the explicit 2026 bounded-obstruction data supports the direct effective finite-search argument recorded here.

value.rationale: The finding upgrades a recent existence theorem to a uniform algorithm deciding every first-order sentence of the existentially closed exponent-three group theory, and isolates the explicit bounded-amalgamation mechanism that makes this possible.
